PS gamers take sophisticated control over passes and shots, setting up the plays, breakaways, and one-timers that could make all the difference between winning the cup and losing the edge. A detailed system for fighting is also included, for those times when the pros feel obliged to seek retaliation outside of the regular rules of the game.

entries.name: NHL 2001 (USA)
entries.description: Featuring the 2000-2001 NHL season, EA Sports returns to the ice with the simulation hockey series, NHL 2001. As in previous editions, the game offers every NHL team (including the Columbus Blue Jackets and the Minnesota Wild), all players, and authentic stadiums. For the game's commentary, making a return in NHL 2001 are Jim Hughson and Bill Clement, who take care of the game's play-by-play and color commentary, respectively.

entries.name: NHL 2000 (USA)
entries.description: This game covers the National Hockey League's 1999-2000 season, with rosters for each NHL team and national team rosters for select hockey nations. It includes the expansion team, Atlanta Thrashers.

entries.name: NHL 99 (USA)
entries.description: Electronic Arts' hockey series returns to PlayStation with new motion-captured animations from actual NHL athletes, a beginner's difficulty setting, on-the-fly play calling strategies, player hot and cold streaks, and revamped goalie artificial intelligence. Play an exhibition game, embark on a full season, jump to the playoffs, enter a tournament, or test your agility in a shootout. You can also work on perfecting your skills during Marc Crawford's coaching drills.

entries.name: NHL 98 (USA)
entries.description: EA SPORTS follows up NHL 97 with their second hockey game on the PlayStation, NHL 98. Based on team and player statistics from the 1996-97 season, NHL 98 introduces a new polygonal game engine designed to increase the speed of play.

entries.name: NHL 97 (USA)
entries.description: Electronic Arts' first hockey game for the PlayStation features 3D polygonal players with authentic names and numbers on their jerseys. In total, there are over 650 players on 26 NHL teams (plus East and West All-Stars) with ratings based on the 1995-96 season.

entries.name: N-Gen Racing (USA)
entries.description: Tired of the same racing games? Cars that travel at a measly 300 mph? How about flying through the course at an amazing 1100 miles per hour? On top of that, try to maintain your balance while you're bombarded with missiles and other weapons by five other fighters. N.GEN Racing has all this and more.

entries.name: NFL Xtreme 2 (USA)
entries.description: Are you ready to slap on the pads and pound the pigskin? NFL Xtreme 2 is the follow-up to 1998's NFL Xtreme, an Arcade-style football game emphasizing trash talking, hard-hitting tackles and penalty-free contests.

entries.name: NFL Xtreme (USA)
entries.description: Like NFL Blitz, NFL Xtreme is football without rules, and features exaggerated tackles, late hits, and high-scoring affairs. To make the action more up-tempo than ordinary football titles, Xtreme uses a five-on-five setup, which puts an emphasis on skilled position players (quarterbacks, running backs, linebackers and cornerbacks).

entries.name: NFL Quarterback Club '97 (USA)
entries.description: NFL Quarterback Club '97 from Acclaim makes a splash on the PlayStation console. Everything you'd expect from a football title can be found in NFL Quarterback Club '97. You have all the standard gameplay options: exhibition, season, quick play. Then you have all the standard options that are looked for in a football game. Players act like their real-life counterpart, complete with juking moves, stiff arms, laterals, diving over the top, and much, much more. Take your favorite team all the way through the season and see if you have what it takes to make it to the Super Bowl, or start from the playoffs altogether.

entries.name: NFL GameDay 2005 (USA)
entries.description: 989 Sports football series returns to the enduring PlayStation for another season in NFL GameDay 2005. This edition features teams, rosters, stats, and uniforms based on the most recent (2003-2004) season. Players can jump in to lead the team of their choice in a quick game, or negotiate and trade for free agents and hot new talent to develop a season-worthy squad with Super Bowl aspirations. Game modes include 'Exhibition,' 'Season,' 'Tournament,' Practice,' and 'General Manager.'

entries.name: NFL GameDay 2004 (USA)
entries.description: Professional football returns to the hardy PlayStation console for another season in NFL GameDay 2004. This edition features teams, rosters, stats, and uniforms based on the most recent (2002-2003) season. Players can jump in to lead the team of their choice in a quick game, or negotiate and trade for free agents and hot new talent to develop a season-worthy squad with Super Bowl aspirations.

entries.name: NFL GameDay 2003 (USA, Canada)
entries.description: Professional football returns to the PlayStation for another season in NFL GameDay 2003. As in the PS2 version of the title, all players and teams from the most recent (2002) season are included here, along with the expansion Houston Texans. Work the field from both sides of the ball to lead your favorite pro team to a victorious season.

entries.name: NFL GameDay 2002 (USA)
entries.description: Sony Computer Entertainment's own 989 football series returns to the hardy PlayStation console with new graphics and features designed to enhance both presentation and gameplay in this release of NFL GameDay 2002. As usual, this year's edition of the game is fully licensed by the NFL and features teams and rosters accurate to the most recent (2000-2001) season.

entries.name: NFL GameDay 2001 (USA)
entries.description: NFL GameDay 2001 continues Sony's football franchise on the PlayStation in this sixth installment of the series. Game commentary and play-by-play are once again handled by Phil Simms and Dick Enberg. Along with the standard modes of play, such as Preseason, Season, General Manager, and Playoffs, there is a new option to play as only one position player while the computer controls the rest of your team. General Manager continues the ability to import college players via a memory card; this time from NCAA GameBreaker 2001.

entries.name: NFL GameDay 2000 (USA)
entries.description: The NFL GameDay series, which made its debut on the PlayStation in 1995, reaches its fifth installment with NFL GameDay 2000. Returning from 1998's NFL GameDay 99 are the 3D polygonal graphics, commentary from Dick Enberg and Phil Simms, support for the Dual Shock Analog Controller and the option to create your own athletes. New features include multiple TV angles, a Play Editor, 200 motion-captured moves and 1,240 plays designed by 32 players from around the league.

entries.name: NFL GameDay 99 (USA) (Rev 1)
entries.description: As the sequel to 1997's #1 selling football game for the Sony PlayStation, NFL GameDay 99 offers several new features designed to improve the gameplay as well as the presentation. First off, the 3D graphics have returned but with double the amount of polygons--bringing the total close to 350 per player. The animations have also improved to deliver one-handed spinning catches, lunges and off-balanced throws. A new zooming camera system will bring you closer to the on-field action, with player photos and statistical updates during the game.

entries.name: NFL GameDay 98 (USA)
entries.description: GameDay '98 is flying onto the sports scene with a major overhaul! New 3D polygon models and motion capturing provided by some of today's hottest NFL players. Animations include high stepping, juking, stiff arm, dive over the pile, and twenty different touchdown dances.

entries.name: NFL GameDay 97 (USA)
entries.description: Grab your pads and helmets and get ready to tackle the sequel to 1995's NFL GameDay. NFL GameDay '97 now features a computer opponent who will learn your play calling tendencies to shut you down. Complete team management is at your fingertips, with the ability to sign free agents, draft and trade players, even create your own star quarterback or punishing lineman. Guide your team through Preseason, Regular Season, Playoffs and the Super Bowl in your quest to become the best.

entries.name: NFL GameDay (USA)
entries.description: Calling all armchair football fanatics -- NFL GameDay brings tackles, fumbles, field goals and touchdowns to your living room with a full National Football League license. Featuring rendered 3D graphics, the developers have crammed over 1,500 actual football players along with 30 NFL teams and their respective stadiums onto a single PlayStation disc. Because of the licensing, each team's logo and end-zone visuals have been represented; jersey colors (both home and away) are authentic to the sport.

entries.name: NFL Full Contact (USA)
entries.description: Konami's first football game on PlayStation features over 1,500 motion-captured players with ratings based on the 1995 season, 30 NFL teams, and moves that include high steps, speed bursts, and spins. Four camera angles let you view the action from the sidelines, high above the stadium, diagonally, or directly behind the activated player. The camera can also be manually zoomed to put you closer to the action. Play one game against the computer or a friend, or go directly to the playoffs (there is no season mode in NFL Full Contact). The opponents you'll face during the playoffs are randomly determined.

entries.name: NFL Blitz 2001 (USA)
entries.description: Midway's popular gridiron pain-fest is back for the 2001 season. NFL Blitz 2001, the third game in the Blitz line for the PlayStation, continues the tradition of the series with the high scoring, the quick playing, and, of course, the excessive violence that has made this football game such a favorite in the arcades and at home.

entries.name: NFL Blitz 2000 (USA)
entries.description: The two teams line up seven per side. It's a typical first and 30 on the initial play from scrimmage. The quarterback snaps the ball only to be pummeled well after the play is over. But there's no flag on the field -- he doesn't even expect one. Why would he when there's no men in zebra-striped shirts (referees) anywhere near the playing field? It's just another day on the gridiron with NFL Blitz 2000.

entries.name: NFL Blitz (USA)
entries.description: From the creators of NBA Jam, NFL Blitz provides football fans with a new way to play their favorite sport. Tired of a measly 10 yards needed for a first down? This game requires 30. Think 11 men per side is too many? Try a seven-on-seven match-up. Hate yelling at the stupid referees? They're gone. In fact, such unsportsmanlike acts as late hits and pass interference are actually encouraged in this game -- anything to keep the other team from scoring. Along with the bone-crunching hits comes an accelerated pace as your real NFL players on their 1998 teams turn on their Turbo meters and play with superhuman abilities.

entries.name: Newman Haas Racing (USA)
entries.description: If you’re looking for an authentic Indy Car experience, get in line for NEWMAN or HAUS RACING. This game offers unprecedented depth and customizability, with an unbelievable variety of options, including 16 real-life Indy drivers, 11 tracks, and four levels of difficulty.

entries.name: Need for Speed - V-Rally (USA)
entries.description: V-Rally '97 features 11 licensed rally vehicles and over 40 tracks with variable weather, terrain, and time of day. Freely adjust such parameters as suspension, gear ratios, and steering before competing in the following three play modes: Arcade, Championship, and Time Trial. Arcade has you advancing through multiple competitions grouped by difficulty, each consisting of four stages. Championship is an eight-race tournament that involves earning points for every top-three finish, while Time Trial lets you compete against the clock or another vehicle.

entries.name: Nectaris - Military Madness (USA)
entries.description: Nectaris: Military Madness is essentially an updated version of the Turbografx-16 classic, Military Madness. The main plot and the original campaign mode was taken straight out of that venerable TG-16 version in fact. (Even the resolution of the combat maps and the music are the same). But the game doesn't just stop where the older version did. Superficially, it adds in the option of polygonal battle cinematics and full motion video sequences. (Purists have the option of using 2D sequences and the impatient can turn off the animations entirely).

entries.name: NCAA March Madness 2001 (USA)
entries.description: The EA Sports' college basketball series NCAA March Madness has established a reputation for realism and diverse gameplay options. NCAA March Madness 2001 builds on this tradition. In addition to the wide range of customizable settings and play modes offered in previous years, the 2001 release of the series offers a new Coach Mode that allows players to guide a team from humble, small-college beginnings all the way to the National Championship game.

entries.name: NCAA March Madness 2000 (USA)
entries.description: Dick Vitale provides color commentary for the sequel to 1999's March Madness with EA SPORTS' NCAA March Madness 2000 for the PlayStation game console. Retaining the similar play style of the previous versions with both Arcade and Simulation modes, March Madness 2000 promises an exciting basketball experience with new motion-captured moves and a Rivalry Mode.

entries.name: NCAA March Madness 99 (USA)
entries.description: Electronic Arts' second college basketball game for the PlayStation expands upon the features first seen in March Madness 98. Now there are over 140 teams to choose from, including 107 Division I men's, 16 top women's (from 1998), 20 historical, and four Electronic Arts teams. The six game modes are as follows: Exhibition, Tournament, Practice, Women's Sweet Sixteen, Three-Point Shootout, and Dynasty. The latter option allows you to guide your favorite team through multiple seasons while filling vacancies left by graduating seniors.

entries.name: March Madness '98 (USA)
entries.description: EA Sports finally hits the college basketball scene with NCAA March Madness '98 for the PlayStation. Along with a full NCAA license is 107 Division I teams, team-specific fight songs and chants as well as authentic college uniforms and logos. Nine women's teams have also been included, which is a first for a college sports game (or any sports game for that matter). Also unique to this game is the Momentum Meter, which will rise as your team starts to get hot. Once it's maxed, look out -- the crowd will become frenzied and your shooting percentage increases.

entries.name: NCAA GameBreaker 2001 (USA)
entries.description: Recreate those Saturday football sessions with 989 Sports' NCAA GameBreaker 2001! With all 115 Division I-A programs intact, this fifth edition features an additional 64 historical teams and 21 bowl games including the Rose Bowl; while each college program is going for championship trophies, individual players will compete for the Heisman Trophy, Sears National Championship Trophy, the All American Team and the Freshman of the Year Award.

entries.name: NCAA GameBreaker 2000 (USA)
entries.description: The fourth game in the annual GameBreaker series for the PlayStation includes 144 Division I-A teams based on the 1998 season, 60 classic teams from yesteryear and multiple college bowl games to heighten the atmosphere. As with the last two games in the series, NCAA GameBreaker 2000 features polygonal graphics, 3D modeled stadiums and multiple camera angles in an attempt to recreate a TV-style presentation.

entries.name: NCAA GameBreaker 99 (USA)
entries.description: Sony Interactive Studios' (renamed 989 Studios in 1998) third college football game for the PlayStation uses the same 3D engine as found in NFL GameDay 99, complete with TV-style camera angles, refined player graphics (now reflecting both height and weight), and 112 NCAA Division I-A teams with accurately modeled stadiums.

entries.name: NCAA GameBreaker 98 (USA)
entries.description: A college football game with three different game styles (simulation, total control, and fantasy league) and three different game types (scrimmage, tournament, and bowl season).

entries.name: NCAA Football GameBreaker (USA)
entries.description: The first college football game released for the PlayStation, NCAA Football GameBreaker includes 111 Division I-A, the top I-AA, and some of the greatest college teams of all-time. Along with the modern teams based on the 1995 season, GameBreaker includes ten Division I-A Conferences such as the BIG 12 and PAC 10. Compete in Exhibition, Season Play with Bowls, Season Play with Tournament, or the National Championship Tournament.

entries.name: NCAA Football 2001 (USA)
entries.description: NCAA Football is back for 2001. This release follows in the long line of respected college football games created by EA Sports, the same company that produces the popular series of Madden NFL games. NCAA Football 2001 features a more comprehensive Dynasty Mode which allows quick reference to the championship ratings. Junior College drafts are available in this version of game. NCAA Football 2001 also boasts improved player control more specific to position, a better running game and more receiver patterns, and improved defensive AI.

entries.name: NCAA Football 2000 (USA) (Rev 1)
entries.description: NCAA Football 2000 continues EA Sports' successful line of college football games with all 114 Division I-A schools and 26 from Division I-AA ready to indulge in the sweetness of a national championship won at the 2000 Nokia Sugar Bowl.

entries.name: NCAA Football 99 (USA)
entries.description: When the leaves start changing color and campuses start filling up, it can only mean one thing: it's time for some college football! Electronic Arts kicks off its second college football game for the PlayStation with all-new 3D polygon graphics, support for the analog controller, on-demand play diagrams and the option to design your own plays.

entries.name: NCAA Football 98 (USA)
entries.description: College football is back in full-effect. Electronic Arts latest, NCAA 98 College Football brings the excitement and thrill of actual college football and puts it in your living room. NCAA 98 features all your favorite college teams, including Nebraska, Arizona State, Georgia Tech, Clemson, Alabama, and more.

entries.name: NCAA Final Four 2001 (USA)
entries.description: NCAA Final Four 2001 continues 989 Studios' college basketball series with updates in a variety of areas. There are now more than 300 division 1-A schools featured from 31 different conferences. Each team will play offensively and defensively true to their real-life counterparts. This year's version also includes more motion-captured moves and player models than previous editions. Quinn Buckner returns for the play-by-play commentary as does the touch shooting meter. Choose your favorite team, earn a berth into the 64-team tournament, and then lead them to the championship.

entries.name: NCAA Final Four 2000 (USA)
entries.description: Feel the excitement of 'March Madness' in the comfort of your own home with NCAA Final Four 2000. Select any of the 300 Division One teams from 31 conferences, including the North Carolina Tarheels, Duke Blue Devils, Michigan State Spartans, and Florida State Seminoles.

entries.name: NCAA Final Four 99 (USA)
entries.description: In 989 Sports' first college basketball game for the PlayStation, NCAA Final Four 99 brings together over 250 Division I teams for play in three game modes: Exhibition, Season or an NCAA 64-team Tournament. Quinn Buckner provides full play-by-play commentary to complement a TV-style presentation with multiple camera angles and a Sixth Man Meter to gauge crowd noise.

entries.name: NCAA Basketball Final Four 97 (USA)
entries.description: NCAA Basketball Final Four '97 brings college hoops home to your Sony PlayStation. 64 big name colleges (such as Kansas, North Carolina, Notre Dame, and Indiana) are represented by team names, logos, and stadiums. Each team is rated according to player statistics. Up to eight people can compete in exhibition play, a 30 game season, or a single elimination six round tournament.

entries.name: NBA Showtime - NBA on NBC (USA)
entries.description: NBA Showtime: NBA on NBC is designed after the NBA Jam series. First, you choose whether or not you want to create a profile for yourself. After that, you choose any team that you wish to compete as. Using your profile, you try to advance your way up through the ranks of the NBA. The team you select can be modified by your choice of players.

entries.name: NBA ShootOut 2004 (USA)
entries.description: NBA ShootOut 2004 continues Sony's basketball series that began in 1995. While the core engine remains the same as in previous versions, the graphics have been touched up in an attempt to deliver more realistic looking players and courts. Once again players can guide their NBA team to victory using the Total Control system for precision passing, screening, dribbling, and shooting, with more than 50 authentic dunks available to finish off a play in style.

entries.name: NBA ShootOut 2003 (USA)
entries.description: 989 Sports once again delivers simulation basketball with NBA ShootOut 2003. Fully sponsored by the NBA, this title features all of the league's teams, arenas, and players on roster as of August 1, 2002. Audio commentary is once again done by Ian Eagle.

entries.name: NBA ShootOut 2002 (USA)
entries.description: Sony's own 989 Sports delivers realistic professional basketball action to the living rooms of PlayStation gamers once again with the release of NBA ShootOut 2002. As usual, the title is fully licensed and uses all of the teams, players, and statistics from the most recent (2000-2001) season. True-to-life player abilities and a variety of actual pro plays are included to provide an authentic dynamic on the court while motion-captured animations enhance the realism of the presentation.

entries.name: NBA ShootOut 2001 (USA)
entries.description: For many seasons, 989's NBA ShootOut Series has competed with EA Sports' NBA Live for the position of top basketball game on the PlayStation market. NBA ShootOut 2001 shows no exception to this tradition. NBA ShootOut 2001 features a redesigned game engine that offers improved gameplay and smoother handling of the enhanced graphics offered by this title. To add to the realism, this game features over 400 motion-captured animations and arenas that are based on the actual stadiums that the NBA teams call home.

entries.name: NBA ShootOut 2000 (USA)
entries.description: NBA Shootout 2000 is the latest basketball game from 989 Sports. Motion-capture is provided by seven real NBA players, bringing the total to a staggering 300 different moves. Every NBA player is included here, along with all their signature moves. Some of the newer basic moves range from the Drop Step to the Killer Crossover.

entries.name: NBA ShootOut 98 (USA)
entries.description: Sony's pro basketball title enters its third season with NBA Shootout 98. The game is quicker than its predecessors, with a focus on bigger action and less realism. An in earlier annual editions of the title, Shootout 98 features the league's 29 teams, each with authentic rosters, arenas, and uniforms. Players are motion-captured for realistic onscreen shots, dunks, and ball handling.

entries.name: NBA Shoot Out '97 (USA)
entries.description: One of the first few games to be developed by SCEE's internal studio, this official basketball simulation is endorsed by the NBA, and features all of the teams from the '97 season. The game features real player likenesses, names and stats. There is also the facility to create customised players.

entries.name: NBA Shoot Out (USA)
entries.description: Sony's first first-party basketball game, NBA Shootout features the league's 29 teams, each with authentic rosters (based on the 1995 season), stadiums and arenas, and uniforms. Ball players have been motion-captured to represent their in-game counterparts; on-screen NBA stars dribble, dish, drive, shoot, and dunk realistically.

entries.name: NBA Live 2003 (USA)
entries.description: EA's NBA Live series returns to the PlayStation, as does announcer Marv Albert, with NBA Live 2003.

entries.name: NBA Live 2002 (USA, Canada)
entries.description: NBA Live 2002 is the 2002 installment of the NBA Live video games series. The cover features Steve Francis of the Houston Rockets. The game was developed by EA Sports and released on November 23, 2001.

entries.name: NBA Live 2001 (USA)
entries.description: NBA Live is back! Enhanced Chat & Match-up with the fast, easy-to-use Match-up System. Improved trade system can involve up to 3 teams and 15 players. Improved 'player personality' means you'll see players argue calls, celebrate a key basket, encourage their teammates, and much more. Also, play the legends such as Michael Jordan in 1-on-1 or 5-on-5 games.

entries.name: NBA Live 2000 (USA)
entries.description: Electronic Arts' long-running hoops series continues with NBA Live 2000 for the PlayStation. This five-on-five contest includes the majority of the players on the rosters of all 29 NBA teams from the 1998-1999 season, including Tim Duncan and Kevin Garnett. For a blast from the past, you can unlock 60 basketball legends, including Larry Bird, 'Magic' Johnson, 'Dr. J', Wilt Chamberlain and Bill Russell. Oh yeah, some guy by the name of Michael Jordan also made the cut. To play as Jordan, you must first beat him in a game of one-on-one.

entries.name: NBA Live 99 (USA)
entries.description: NBA Live is back on the PlayStation and this time it includes such features as multiple seasons and a practice mode. You can also hit the hardwood in either the faster paced Arcade mode or the more realistic Simulation mode. While all of the NBA teams and ballplayers are here, user options allow athletes to be drafted, signed, traded, created, and released. NBA Live 99 also includes play-by-play speech and motion-captured moves.

entries.name: NBA Live 98 (USA)
entries.description: NBA Live '98 brings the furious action of 5 on 5 basketball to the Playstation. A fully licensed product, this title includes all 29 NBA teams from the 1997-'98 season. Featuring user-controlled dunking and passing, a wide variety of moves, and players who actually look like their real-life counterparts. NBA Live '98 supports up to 8 players via Multi-Tap, so you can play with ALL of your friends. When the action gets too intense, you can challenge either the computer or your friends (or both) to the 3-point shoot out contest.

entries.name: NBA Live 97 (USA)
entries.description: With a solid reputation preceding it, the NBA Live series is one of the most respected in the video game industry. After a solid showing on the Super NES and Genesis, EA Sports took to the latest hardware, the Sony Playstation. Last years NBA Live title delivered everything that fans of the series has come to expect.

entries.name: NBA Live 96 (USA)
entries.description: Officially licensed and endorsed by the National Basketball Association, NBA Live 96 features all 29 NBA teams in addition to two All Star teams and over 300 real players and rosters based on the 1995 season. Additionally, each team's home courts have been faithfully represented with realistic detailing.

entries.name: NBA Jam - Tournament Edition (USA)
entries.description: NBA Jam T.E. features 2-on-2 fast-paced and unrealistic basketball. Following in the tradition of NBA Jam this game is filled with super dunks and has no out-of-bounds. Also featured are 9-point plays, rookie and all-star teams, injuries, and fatigue. A variety of power-ups allow: monster jams from anywhere, speed increase, power increase, unlimited turbo, increased 3-point ability, catch fire, and a bomb that flattens all of the other players.

entries.name: NBA Jam Extreme (USA)
entries.description: Acclaim's over-the-top, two-on-two basketball series moves into the 3D realm with NBA Jam Extreme. The core play mechanics are identical to previous titles in the NBA Jam series, with acrobatic dunks, authentic players, and fast-paced action viewed from a side-scrolling perspective.

entries.name: NBA in the Zone 2000 (USA)
entries.description: The third in the In the Zone titles features all the usual options you come to expect from an NBA simulation title, including Season, Exhibition, Playoff, All-Star, Slam Dunk and three point shoot-out contests.

entries.name: NBA in the Zone '99 (USA)
entries.description: Konami's fourth basketball game for the PlayStation brings together 29 NBA teams and over 300 authentic players with ratings based on the 1997-98 season. Added features include a 50-game schedule, NBA arena announcer Ray Clay, new motion-captured animations, and both three-point and slam dunk contests. As in previous games, the camera can be switched to different angles and zoomed in or out to offer multiple views of the court.

entries.name: NBA in the Zone '98 (USA) (Rev 1)
entries.description: Coming back for its third straight season, NBA In the Zone '98 walks onto the court ready to go. Konami went back to the drawing board for the lastest incarnation into the series, adding new feature after new feature. Want real moves? You've got them.

entries.name: NBA in the Zone 2 (USA)
entries.description: Get ready to run the floors with NBA In the Zone 2 from Konami. After last years title, Konami has stepped up and added new features to ITZ2 to make it the best possible basketball game. Featuring different play modes such as exhibition and full season play, as well as containing full rosters for all the NBA teams and the ability to make substitutions, ITZ2 is loaded.

entries.name: NBA in the Zone (USA)
entries.description: This is the first in the NBA in the Zone games, which is considered a true simulation of the NBA. There are 29 teams to choose from with a full compliment of rosters from the 1996 season and a plethora of offensive and defensive plays to use against their opponents with trick shots like behind-the-back passes, skyhooks, alley-oops, fade-away jumpers and of course the slam dunk.

entries.name: NBA Hoopz (USA)
entries.description: NBA Hoopz takes an extreme approach to the sport of basketball, in terms of both gameplay and presentation. Just as Midway's NFL Blitz caricatures football with exaggerated personality and arcade-style gameplay, NBA Hoopz presents professional basketball with an emphasis on fast action and amazing plays at the expense of strict rules or an overly sophisticated interface. This game is similar in spirit to Acclaim's NBA Jam series, though NBA Hoopz focuses on 3-on-3 action instead of Acclaim's 2-on-2 format.

entries.name: NBA Hangtime (USA)
entries.description: NBA Hang Time is a two-on-two hoops contest in the tradition of NBA Jam and NBA Jam T.E. Choose from 29 NBA teams and 145 professional stars with ratings based on the 1995-96 season, or create your own players and save them directly to memory card. Customize your athlete's head, uniform, attributes, or name, and then build his ratings by winning games or correctly answering trivia questions. Sixteen different heads allow you to create offbeat characters such as aliens or clowns.

entries.name: NBA Fastbreak '98 (USA)
entries.description: Select your favorite pro basketball team and compete in an exhibition game, practice session, or complete season with NBA Fastbreak '98. The game includes 29 NBA teams with an option to view the on-court action from 11 different camera angles. Lead your motion-captured athletes on a scoring spree with 27 offensive sets.

entries.name: NBA Basketball 2000 (USA)
entries.description: Updated with stats, rosters and player ratings for the 1999-2000 season, NBA Basketball 2000 features every player from all 29 NBA teams, plus two all-star and rookie teams. You can play an entire NBA season or skip ahead to the playoffs. If you're not ready for team ball, you can go one-on-one with your favorite pros on an outdoor court. Real Fox Sports announcers including former Atlanta Hawks point guard Doc Rivers, call the action.

entries.name: NASCAR Thunder 2004 (USA)
entries.description: NASCAR Thunder returns to PlayStation with all 23 authentic Winston Cup venues and 11 new fantasy tracks. The Career mode features a redesigned interface as players strive to develop relationships with sponsors, crews, and research teams during a span of 20 years. Aggressive drivers will no longer be tolerated in the game, with computer opponents aiming for retaliation if players cut them off or brush against them during the heat of the race. The consequences of wrecks are also more apparent in this version, as errant cars flip, ricochet, and bounce back into the field of play before bursting into flames.

entries.name: NASCAR Thunder 2003 (USA)
entries.description: NASCAR Thunder 2003 for PlayStation offers NASCAR Winston Cup fans Quick Race, Single Race, Season, and Thunder Plate challenge modes, customizable car skins, enhanced stability control and auto-braking, and multiple gameplay options. Ten fantasy road courses and a 1950s Daytona Beach track complement 23 regular NASCAR circuits, with action for up to two players in head-to-head competition.

entries.name: NASCAR Thunder 2002 (USA, Canada)
entries.description: EA SPORTS invites gamers to return to the tracks for a fully redesigned 3D stock car racing experience in NASCAR Thunder 2002. As development responsibilities of EA's annual NASCAR release move to the latter-day Madden NFL designers at Tiburon Entertainment, the title is reinforced with the word 'Thunder' in honor of the game's extensive revisions and the series' new direction.

entries.name: NASCAR Rumble (USA, Canada)
entries.description: Did you ever want to take control of over 750 horses and drive 200 M.P.H. on twisting, open-road courses through the heart of America? You now have your chance with NASCAR Rumble for the PlayStation from EA SPORTS. Race Arcade-style in tricked out cars as one of nearly 40 NASCAR stock car and truck drivers, including Jeff Gordon, Dale Jarrett, Tony Stewart and Dale Earnhardt. After winning a championship race, you can even challenge the courses as 'The King' Richard Petty, Benny Parsons or five other NASCAR legends.

entries.name: NASCAR Racing (USA)
entries.description: Nascar Racing features drivers based on their real-life counterparts from the 1996 Nascar season. Included are three modes of play -- arcade, simulation, and simulation testing -- and a variety of options. Simulation options available are: turn on or off driving aids, adjust tire pressure, adjust wheel settings, adjust aerodynamics, change gear settings, adjust shocks, angle cross weight, angle spoiler, and set wheel stagger.

entries.name: NASCAR Heat (USA)
entries.description: NASCAR Heat is a racing game designed to appeal to both hardcore race fans and casual gamers alike. The game features several unique challenges and options to adjust realism and playability. The game's physics model has two settings for play: Normal mode and Expert mode. At the Normal setting, players can focus on basic steering and jockeying for position against other cars on the track, leaving some of the more sophisticated car-handling concerns out of the mix. The physics model becomes much more realistic in the Expert mode and players must compensate for many of the environmental and inertial factors that influence real drivers on real courses.

entries.name: NASCAR 2001 (USA)
entries.description: This '2001' version of EA Sports' NASCAR is built on a new game engine, designed to produce improved environment mapping, real-time lighting effects, and realistic car physics. It is also the first NASCAR game to allow virtual drivers to race the quintessential Daytona 500. Over two dozen other ovals and road courses are available, as well, and the game features all 34 real-life drivers and teams from the most recent full season. Players can race through multiple seasons in the game, customizing their vehicles and building a reputation for precision driving at 200+ MPH.

entries.name: NASCAR 2000 (USA)
entries.description: Do you like to race cars? Ever feel the need for speed? If you answered yes to the above questions, NASCAR 2000 by EA Sports fulfills that need! By taking on the personalities of one of over forty real-life NASCAR drives, you'll become what you've always wanted to be -- a racecar driver. But if you'd rather create your own driving persona, that's cool too. Players are given an option to create their likeness in the Create-A-Driver mode; choose any car and modifications you'd like and you're ready to go!

entries.name: NASCAR 99 Legacy (USA)
entries.description: Driver personalities, tense fender-to-fender tactics, and the white-knuckle anxiety of NASCAR's circuit speeds onto the PS in NASCAR 99. Features include 37 real-life cars (24 on the track in any given race), 17 licensed tracks, night racing, split-screen mode for two-player action, and single race or seasonal gameplay modes. Driver statistics are based on the 1997 season, and the NASCAR point system is utilized to track standings. Skilled driving in Championship mode will unlock legendary drivers like Bobby Allison, Cale Yarborough, and Richard Petty.

entries.name: NASCAR 99 (USA)
entries.description: Driver personalities, tense fender-to-fender tactics, and the white-knuckle anxiety of NASCAR's circuit speeds onto the PS in NASCAR 99. Features include 37 real-life cars (24 on the track in any given race), 17 licensed tracks, night racing, split-screen mode for two-player action, and single race or seasonal gameplay modes. Driver statistics are based on the 1997 season, and the NASCAR point system is utilized to track standings. Skilled driving in Championship mode will unlock legendary drivers like Bobby Allison, Cale Yarborough, and Richard Petty.

entries.name: NASCAR 98 Collector's Edition (USA)
entries.description: Racing at a speed of over 200 miles per hour isn't legal on the interstate. But you can do it all you want on your television screen in NASCAR 98.

entries.name: NASCAR 98 (USA)
entries.description: Racing at a speed of over 200 miles per hour isn't legal on the interstate. But you can do it all you want on your television screen in NASCAR 98.

entries.name: NanoTek Warrior (USA)
entries.description: Nanotek Warrior is probably based (or at least inspired) in the classic Spectrum (and other 8 bits platforms) game Eliminator released and development by Hewson Consultants Ltd.

entries.name: Namco Museum Vol. 5 (USA)
entries.description: Namco has been on a roll ever since the company released its first Namco Museum title. Now, in the series' fifth installment, Namco has included some fairly recent titles (if you consider the 1980's recent) while still digging deep into the retro gaming vault to pull out a classic sleeper hit or two.

entries.name: Namco Museum Vol. 4 (USA)
entries.description: With three compilation discs under their belt, Namco once again gives gamers a dose of classic Arcade nostalgia. Namco Museum Vol. 4 includes five games: Assault, Pac-Land, The Return of Ishtar, Ordyne and The Genji and the Heike Clans. Each title has been replicated in its entirety to look, play and sound like the originals on which they are based.

entries.name: Namco Museum Vol. 3 (USA)
entries.description: Namco Museum Vol. 3 offers up six more coin-op classics from the vaults of gaming's distant past. Titles include Ms. Pac-Man, Dig Dug, Galaxian, Pole Position II, Phozon and The Tower of Druaga. In addition to the games, this collection contains a museum in which you can view collectible videogame items (relevant to the games on this disc) such as screen overlays, advertisements and merchandise.

entries.name: Namco Museum Vol. 2 (USA)
entries.description: Namco Museum vol.2 is the second, and arguably hardest-to-find, title in the Namco Museum series for the PS1, this volume packs in arcade favorites like Mappy, Xevious and Super Pac-Man, along with lesser-known sequels Gaplus (a lightning-fast Galaga sequel, better known to U.S. gamers as Galaga 3) and Grobda (a ground-based follow-up to Xevious) and the quest-style Dragon Buster. The menu, option selection and control structure is very much the same as Namco Museum Volume 1, making it a bit difficult to navigate (something later refined in Namco Museum Volume 3).

entries.name: Namco Museum Vol. 1 (USA) (Rev 1)
entries.description: Collecting seven early to mid 1980s videogames on one CD, Namco Museum Vol. 1 includes: Pac-Man, the first-ever cute character maze game; Galaga, a Space Invaders-influenced shooter featuring a star fighter versus wave after wave of alien spaceships; Pole Position, the first car racing game where you must qualify before beginning the main race; Bosconian, an Asteroids-like shoot 'em up; Rally-X and New Rally-X, car racing maze games in which you use smoke screens to wipe out other vehicles; and Toy Pop, a game set in a whimsical world of presents and toys.

entries.name: Nagano Winter Olympics '98 (USA)
entries.description: Nagano Winter Olympics 98 is a follow up to Konami's briliant International Track & Field. With more than thirteen events including speed skating short track 500 and 1000m, speed skating 1500 and 500m, Alpine Skiing Downhill and Giant Slalom, Aerial, Curling, Ski Jump, Bobsled, Luge Snowboard and Alpine Skiing Super G. Luckily the game supports multi tap allowing for up to four players to take up competition head on and the game was made to be easily picked up by casual gamers.

entries.name: N2O - Nitrous Oxide (USA)
entries.description: Your mission in N2O: Nitrous Oxide is simple: Fly a ship called a tunnel runner into nitrous oxide filled tubes, and destroy the enemies they hold within. These enemies are mutated insects, including beetles, mosquitoes, flies and wasps. For each enemy you kill, your runner increases in speed.

entries.name: Myst (USA)
entries.description: Had you known the consequences of picking up the mysterious old book, you would have never touched it. But you were curious; naïvely thinking this was an ordinary periodical. As you flip through the pages, the storyteller presents a beautiful image of perfect landscapes in a lush world. You are enthralled with a sense of immersion, as if the world is becoming real. Slowly, the real world dissolves and you find yourself standing on a pier facing an island.

entries.name: My Disney Kitchen (USA)
entries.description: Originally released by Disney Interactive in 1998 as a hybrid title for the Macintosh and PC, My Disney Kitchen gets re-cooked for the PlayStation, courtesy of BAM! Entertainment. Young chefs learn how to prepare various dishes, create meals and experiment with zany appliances, and acquire a practical sense of cleaning up after finished. More than 30 recipes are provided by FamilyFun Magazine, utilizing a fully stocked refrigerator and pantry in My Disney Kitchen. Gameplay encourages experimentation with ingredients, setting the table, arranging the room, serving food, and topping off concoctions with syrup, berries, and more.

entries.name: Muppet RaceMania (USA)
entries.description: Muppet RaceMania is a kart-racer for the PlayStation console. Starring the likes of the loveable Kermit the frog, the violent but always sweet Miss Piggy, Fozzie Bear, whose inspiration for racing is to make it the other side, the human cannonball Gonzo, Rizzo the Rat, who enjoys an occasional slice of cheese and likes nothing more than pulling obnoxious one-liners, the wild thing Animal, as well as Rowlf, Beaker, Dr. Bunsen Honeydew, Scooter, Sam The Eagle, the groovester Floyd Pepper and even those grumpy old men, meaning all of your favorites are here.

entries.name: Muppet Monster Adventure (USA)
entries.description: Kermit and friends have agreed to go with Doctor Honeydew so he can attend his late Uncle Petry's will ceremony. The problem is that the house appears evil, and they begin to tremble as they knock on the door. Suddenly, Kermit's nephew Robin passes out from sheer terror as he sees a dark figure.

entries.name: MTV Sports - T.J. Lavin's Ultimate BMX (USA)
entries.description: Two-time ESPN X-Games gold medal winner T. J. Lavin lends his name and expertise to this stunt bike game from MTV Sports. The game features BMX stunt riding on the street, off road, and in special parks.
entries.rom_name: MTV Sports - T.J. Lavin's Ultimate BMX (USA).bin

entries.name: MTV Sports - Snowboarding (USA)
entries.description: MTV Sports: Snowboarding is a 3D snowboarding game for the Sony Playstation. This CD-ROM features fast, real-life mountain runs and plenty of licensed music tracks for you to listen to while playing.

entries.name: MTV Sports Skateboarding Featuring Andy MacDonald (USA)
entries.description: MTV Sports Skateboarding featuring Andy McDonald is the first game from the MTV Sports line, and like Tony Hawk's Pro Skater, it combines real elements of the sport with fantastic tricks and parks that would be impossible to recreate in real life.
entries.rom_name: MTV Sports Skateboarding Featuring Andy MacDonald (USA).cue

entries.name: MTV Sports - Pure Ride (USA)
entries.description: MTV Sports: Pure Ride is a multi-event snowboarding game that brings trick and stunt action, as well as high-speed downhill jaunts, to the PlayStation. The game contains a number of different snowboarding characters from around the world -- most of them are fictitious, and some are quite wacky in their design. -- and a variety of boards for snow shredding. Each rider and board has his or her (or its) own strengths and weaknesses.

entries.name: MTV Music Generator (USA)
entries.description: The MTV Music Generator is a simulator for making custom music tracks for your PlayStation. Developed by Jester Interactive and published by The Codemasters Software Company, this mouse-compatible music generator allows you to create and save music tracks with special sound effects like chorus, tempo and reverb for infinite possibilities.

entries.name: MTV Celebrity Deathmatch (USA)
entries.description: Music Television's satirical Claymation-style series comes alive on home computers and next-gen consoles in this release from Gotham Games. Players can choose to enter the fray as one of over 20 different 3D celebrity caricatures, including favorites from past shows and a few that make their debut in this game.

entries.name: Ms. Pac-Man Maze Madness (USA) (Rev 1)
entries.description: Pac-Land is protected by the four gems of virtue: Generosity, Truth, Wisdom, and Courage. These four gems are scattered in the four Wonders of Pac-Land, mystical regions separated from Pac-Land by mysterious force fields. The gems are in place to keep darkness and chaos from falling on Pac-Land.

entries.name: Mr. Driller (USA)
entries.description: Mr. Driller loves to drill. So when Downtown was mysteriously overrun with colored blocks, he was the obvious choice to get to the bottom of the situation. Armed with his trusty jackhammer, he begins his descent toward the Earth's core.

entries.name: Motorhead (USA)
entries.description: Motorhead is a futuristic racing title featuring a total of ten playable cars on eight twisting courses, ranging from an industrial area to a desert. Each vehicle is individually rated in speed, acceleration, and grip. There are no weapons or power-ups to collect; it's just you, a friend, or the computer competing for the fastest time. Four play modes include Time Attack, League, Head-to-Head, and Single Race. Each mode offers the option to view the action at 30 or 60 frames per second, with the key difference being the number of computer-controlled cars on the track.

entries.name: Motor Toon Grand Prix (USA)
entries.description: The original Motor Toon Grand Prix was only released in Japan, a creative racer that never really eventuated due to lacking gameplay. Motor Toon GP 2 is an imaginative cartoony roller coaster race set in a number of wacky worlds with strong similarities between a mix of Mario Kart and Wipeout.

entries.name: Motocross Mania 2 (USA)
entries.description: Motocross Mania 2 brings the reckless action of motocross racing back to the PlayStation. Players will experience improved turning, refined graphics, advanced bikes, new stunts, two classes of bikes (125cc or 250cc), and three levels of difficulty spread across 16 tracks. Devoted motocross racers can develop their own tracks with the Edit Track option.

entries.name: Motocross Mania (USA)
entries.description: Catch big air or eat big dust in this arcade-style dirt bike game from Take 2. In Motocross Mania players choose their machines and fine-tune them to match riding styles, then enter Motocross, Supercross, and freestyle competitions for cash prizes. Prize money can be used to purchase performance-enhancing upgrades. As virtual riders progress through increasingly difficult contests, new tracks, tricks and motorbikes become unlocked and available for use.

entries.name: Moto Racer World Tour (USA)
entries.description: Delphine Software presents Moto Racer World Tour, the third installment in the company's successful series of motorcycle racing games. Building upon the well-received features of Moto Racer and Moto Racer 2, Moto Racer World Tour allows players to race both street and dirt bikes, and to use the included track-editor to design their own challenges. A thorough list of options lets players customize the gameplay to their liking, allowing for arcade-style speed and fun or a more realistic simulation of motorcycle racing. New in this version of the game are over thirty race courses, all of them based on real-life locations.

entries.name: Moto Racer 2 (USA)
entries.description: If you thought Moto Racer was good, prepare yourself for Moto Racer 2 because this Motor Cycle/Dirt Bike game is not for the faint hearted.

entries.name: Moto Racer (USA)
entries.description: The PC Smash hit Moto Racer has finally found itself wound up on the Playstation and while the visuals have dropped down a few notchs, the conversion all round has been handled well.

entries.name: Mortal Kombat Trilogy (USA) (Rev 1)
entries.description: The second Mortal Kombat game on PlayStation combines characters, stages, and moves from earlier installments in the violent fighting series. Choose from a total of 36 playable characters, including alternate versions of Kano, Jax, Raiden, Sub-Zero, and Kung Lao. As in previous games, you must fight and defeat each opponent in succession in your quest to confront the evil Shao Khan. Each match is a best-of-three contest that involves depleting a rival's health, at which point you can initiate a character-specific '-ality' move: fatality, animality, babality, or brutality.

entries.name: Mortal Kombat - Special Forces (USA)
entries.description: Why do people hate? What causes such intense animosity that a person would go to any length to hurt someone, perhaps even destroy them? These are just a few questions posed by the relationship of Jax and Kano.

entries.name: Mortal Kombat Mythologies - Sub-Zero (USA)
entries.description: Midway decided to do something a little different with its Mortal Kombat franchise. They decided rather than to make a whole new MK game, they'd make a game that focused on one particular character from the popular series; a mini MK if you will. They'd shine some light on his past and present gamers with a story, rather than mindless fights to win a tournament. The character of choice is Sub Zero, and the game is aptly titled Mortal Kombat Mythologies: Sub Zero.

entries.name: Mortal Kombat 4 (USA)
entries.description: In an attempt to save Earth, Raiden began a war with Shinnok, a fallen Elder God, and his minions; a decision that cost many people their lives. The battle raged on for thousands of years and many tournaments were held to find out who was the strongest combatant. The winner would then face the ultimate challenge of defeating one of Shinnok's disciples. After the Earth warriors were successful in overcoming his strongest adversary, the evil god Shao Kahn escaped the Netherealm for one last-ditch effort at world supremacy.

entries.name: Mortal Kombat 3 (USA)
entries.description: Unclear as to what happened at the end of Mortal Kombat II? The answer is: more Komabt! Mortal Kombat 3 is the third gruesome installment of the game infuriating congressmen everywhere. After the Kombatants lost the second tournament in Outworld, alternate-dimensional home of baddie Shao Kahn and his sorcerer Shang Tsung, Kahn decided to take over the Earth like any steroid-poppin' supervillian would. Conquering the souls of all but a few select Earthlings, Kahn prepares warriors of his own to meet the likes of Liu Kang and Sub-Zero head on.

entries.name: Mortal Kombat 3 (USA)
entries.description: Unclear as to what happened at the end of Mortal Kombat II? The answer is: more Komabt! Mortal Kombat 3 is the third gruesome installment of the game infuriating congressmen everywhere. After the Kombatants lost the second tournament in Outworld, alternate-dimensional home of baddie Shao Kahn and his sorcerer Shang Tsung, Kahn decided to take over the Earth like any steroid-poppin' supervillian would. Conquering the souls of all but a few select Earthlings, Kahn prepares warriors of his own to meet the likes of Liu Kang and Sub-Zero head on.

entries.name: Mort the Chicken (USA)
entries.description: Chickens, which happen to be the dominant form of life on a mysterious planet, are in trouble. Block creatures from another world have emerged from a well to kidnap all the baby chicks! In an act of pure courage, Mort the Chicken dove into the well after them. Mort, of course, is not your average chicken: he has super powers. Now you must help him cluck, glide, peck and comb-whip his way through the block creatures' world and lead the chicks safely back to the farm.

entries.name: MonsterSeed (USA)
entries.description: In Monsterseed, players assume the role of Daniel, a young 'ruler' who begins the game by getting himself beaten unconscious, but is rescued by the lovely Kal and her rugged grandfather, Wolf. Daniel learns that the thugs who attacked him are part of an evil gang terrorizing his benefactors' little town. The gang's leader Murdoch is collecting ancient statues to open a gateway to the Dark World, hoping to resurrect an immensely powerful monster. Driven by a sense of duty to repay and protect Wolf and Kal, Daniel pursues Murdoch through labyrinthine mines and ruins, a booby-trapped mansion, and even through the Dark World itself, fighting wild monsters and collecting monster seeds along the way.

entries.name: Monster Rancher 2 (USA)
entries.description: The first Monster Rancher was a cult hit among players of all ages. Monster Rancher 2, released two years later, retains the basic premise of the original while adding several new features and more advanced graphics.

entries.name: Monster Rancher Hop-A-Bout (USA)
entries.description: Tecmo expands its Monster Rancher line with Monster Rancher Hop-A-Bout for the PlayStation. This game is a fast-paced platform jumper in which players race their bouncing characters through extraordinary obstacle courses. Along the way there are several panels which can provide all sorts of power-ups to the characters that find them.

entries.name: Monster Rancher Battle Card - Episode II (USA)
entries.description: Monster Rancher Battle Card: Episode II is set in the Monster Rancher universe, but instead of raising and battling monsters, players collect cards from around the game world and use them to build decks, taking on opponents in order to snag even more of the precious collectables.
entries.rom_name: Monster Rancher Battle Card - Episode II (USA) (Track 1).bin

entries.name: Monster Rancher (USA)
entries.description: What would it be like to own a ranch and breed your very own monster? You would raise your monster from a little baby, build up his physical and mental attributes, have him compete in fighting tournaments for fame and recognition and have him go on various side quests to help find treasures. You would punish him for acting dishonorably around people and accommodate him with monster treats for jobs well done.

entries.name: Monster Bass (USA)
entries.description: Monster Bass! is a fishing simulator set in four locations. The player gets to control the bait to lure and catch several types of 'scientifically mutated gigantic monster bass'. As the game progresses special baits and tricks get unlocked.

entries.name: Monopoly (USA) (Alt)
entries.description: The game of Monopoly has been around ever since the Great Depression-era of the 1920s. The PlayStation version of the game boasts token and property animations, rule variations, real-time board rotation and multi-player link options.

entries.name: Monkey Magic (USA)
entries.description: Since the dawn of time, the Celestial Heavens have been home to powerful beings who seek to create balance and peace in the entire universe. But there is never good without evil. Dearth Voyd, the Lord of Chaos, strives to bring war and violence to the universe. These two forces have been at odds forever with each being equal to the other, never gaining ground, and never truly winning the war. That is until the Stone Monkey Kongo came along.

entries.name: Monkey Hero (USA)
entries.description: The Waking World, Dream World and Nightmare World all coexisted long ago to maintain harmony among all living things. This careful balance was ensured by the Magic Storybook of Dreams, preventing those who lived in the Nightmare World from entering the other two worlds and filling them with despair.

entries.name: Monaco Grand Prix (USA)
entries.description: Monaco Grand Prix brings Formula One racing to the PlayStation with 16 different tracks and four modes of play. Each track is modeled after its real life counterpart and includes the famous Monaco circuit, Australia, Japan, Great Britain, Brazil, Italy, Canada, Germany, France, Argentina, and Spain. Players can race these tracks in a single race, time attack, championship, or arcade mode.

entries.name: Mobile Light Force (USA)
entries.description: Gunbird is a vertically scrolling shoot 'em up released in 1994 by Japanese company Psikyo. It was followed by a sequel, Gunbird 2, in 1998. The first game was released in the United States and Europe as Mobile Light Force for the PlayStation.

entries.name: Mobile Armor (USA)
entries.description: Featuring ten tanks from World War II, Mobile Armor is a mission-based shooter in which you control the 'Mars army tank' in battle against a succession of 'Earth army tanks.' Completed missions in single-player story mode become available for two-player free mode, with one player manning the cannons and the other the tank, as well as for two-player VS mode. In VS mode, five tanks are available from cleared story mode missions, with another five added based on the number of cumulative defeated Earth army tanks.

entries.name: Mobil 1 Rally Championship (USA)
entries.description: Europe's premiere rally racing championship is showcased in Electronic Arts' Mobil 1 Rally Championship. Developed by the U.K.'s Magnetic Fields with help from Hot Gen, the game offers a realistic simulation of the Official British Rally Championship on a wild ride through the lush British countryside on over 400 miles of track. The game offers both on and off road segments, including English country roads and over 20 licensed cars to choose from. Highly detailed weather effects and realistic car damage (that effects you car's performance) add to the immersive gameplay.

entries.name: MLB Pennant Race (USA)
entries.description: The makers of NFL GameDay tackle the diamond with MLB Pennant Race, Sony's first baseball game for PlayStation. Choose from 28 Major League teams and take a swing at five play modes: Exhibition, Season, World Series, Playoffs, and Home Run Derby. Over 700 real players are included with statistics and ratings based on the 1995 season. Key features include commentary from broadcaster Jerry Coleman, three difficulty settings, and stat tracking for 16 categories on offense and defense. Management options include trades, free agents, custom players, and multiple defensive formations.

entries.name: MLB 2005 (USA)
entries.description: Sony's 989 Sports returns to the diamond to pitch the '2004' installment of its Major League Baseball series, available for both PS2 and the hardy, original PlayStation. This year's game brings home a variety of modes, offering Exhibition, Season, Franchise, and Career play, as well as Spring Training. Authentic teams and rosters are based on the most recent (2003) season.

entries.name: MLB 2004 (USA)
entries.description: The national pastime returns home to the PlayStation in 989 Sports' MLB 2004. Like it's teammate on the PS2, this year's PS baseball sim features all the teams and players from the most recent (2002) Major League Baseball season. Motion-captured animations and detailed virtual stadiums are designed to bring the game to life.

entries.name: MLB 2003 (USA)
entries.description: The only baseball game released for the PlayStation in 2002, MLB 2003 continues Sony's seven-year franchise with updated teams, schedules, and rosters to reflect the beginning of the 2002 season. Eight modes of play include Quick Start, Exhibition, All-Star Game, Season, Playoffs, World Series, Spring Training, and Home Run Derby. The Season mode supports one or two players and offers both a Franchise and Manager option to further customize the action.

entries.name: MLB 2002 (USA)
entries.description: Choose a favorite team and guide its players all the way to the World Series in this rendition of America's favorite pastime. Well over a dozen Major League ballplayers were consulted to help create the most realistic artificial intelligence possible. MLB 2002 features more than 300 motion-captured animations, and the athletes are modeled after their real-life counterparts. Over 250 signature moves add to the game's realism by making the virtual players easily recognizable to their gaming fans.

entries.name: MLB 2001 (USA)
entries.description: 989 Sports is back for Major League Baseball's 2000 season! This marks the fifth installment of a series that originated with MLB Pennant Race, and the same batter-pitcher interface used in the three previous titles can be found in this one. So what are you waiting for? It's time for MLB 2001 on the PlayStation!

entries.name: MLB 2000 (USA)
entries.description: As the sequel to 1998's MLB 99, MLB 2000 features an expanded Spring Training mode, new 3D player models with authentic faces and over 175 actual batting stances. Also featured are updated stadiums to reflect details such as the moving fountains at Kauffman Stadium and the outfield monuments at Yankee Stadium, and a new color-commentator in ESPN's Dave Campbell. Returning to the game are the Season (with a 1999 schedule), All-Star Game, Playoffs, Home Run Derby, Exhibition and Spring Training modes of play.

entries.name: MLB 99 (USA)
entries.description: Sony's MLB 99 offers a number of options to set it apart from most games based on the national pastime. The first advancement is a Spring Training mode. This involves creating a player at any position and nurturing him in spring training; if he does well both in the field and at the plate, he'll earn points.

entries.name: MLB 98 (USA)
entries.description: Sony Interactive's MLB 98 represents a significant departure from 1996's MLB Pennant Race, the company's first baseball game on the PlayStation. Players in this game are now made up of polygons, making the transition into 3D, and there is a new cursor option to go along with the traditional timing method used to hit the ball. In addition to the new 3D players and authentic stadiums, more animation has been included to show fluid catches, dives, slides and throws -- even from the knees!

entries.name: Mission - Impossible (USA) (En,Fr,Es)
entries.description: Good morning, Mr. Phelps... there's a slew of spies, terrorists, international arms dealers and undercover agents secretly committing their heinous trades in order to prevent world peace. Your mission, if you decide to accept it, is to take on the role of Ethan Hunt, Impossible Mission Force's (IMF's) top agent and point man. You'll be supplied with the agency's special weaponry and equipment at your disposal to carry out your classified Mission: Impossible for the PlayStation, courtesy of Infogrames.

entries.name: Missile Command (USA)
entries.description: Prepare for launch! Prepare for defense! Prepare for your potential battle of a lifetime!

entries.name: Miss Spider's Tea Party (USA)
entries.description: Based on the award-winning book by David Kirk, Miss Spider's Tea Party offers young children eight games that encourage cognitive thinking skills. Miss Spider is featured inviting her insect friends to a tea party, which they cannot attend until their posed dilemmas are solved. Choosing the order of invite, children help characters like Grampy Spider and Mr. Ant solve their problem and attend the tea party.

entries.name: Miracle Space Race (USA)
entries.description: Miracle Space Racing is a racing game in the style of crash bandicoot racing or Mario kart games in the Nintendo.

entries.name: Mike Tyson Boxing (USA) (En,Fr,Es)
entries.description: Mike Tyson Boxing is a 3D simulation based on one of the best-known fighters of the '80s and '90s. The game offers three main modes of play: 'Vs.' mode offers fast, arcade-style matches in which the loser walks and the winner stays on to meet the next challenger. 'Showcase' mode allows up to eight players and eight CPU boxers to meet for rotating tournament action. In 'World' mode, the player starts with a rookie fighter and guides his career fight after fight through the ranks of contenders until he finally faces the champ for the belt. Mike Tyson Boxing features over 90 different boxers and 16 world-class venues.

entries.name: FoxKids.com - Micro Maniacs Racing (USA)
entries.description: Since saving the world from the impending food shortage is a tall order, our good friend Dr. Minimizer sets out to cajole, blackmail and create participants to compete for the right to lead the colonization of Earth once everyone's been shrunk to 1/30th their original size.

entries.name: Micro Machines V3 (USA)
entries.description: Micro Machines is back bigger and better than ever. With over 48 tracks set over exciting miniature worlds such as pool tables, outback gardens, science labs, and even picnic tables. Tracks are also now all full 3D with amazing visual effects just to make your mouth water. Also featuring intense multi player action rated by many as the Playstations number one multi player title.

entries.name: Michelin Rally Masters - Race of Champions (USA) (En,Fr,Es)
entries.description: As the only WRC-sanctioned game to allow one-on-one gameplay, Michelin Rally Masters Race of Champions features 30 real drivers from the past, present, and future of the sport. Players can choose from over 17 authentic vehicles from real-life manufacturers like Ford, Peugot, Lancia, Renualt, Toyota, and others. There are four modes of gameplay on 46 different tracks, with the option of day or night racing under clear skies or in ice, rain, snow, or fog. Real-time collision damage is graphically represented and there is an option to allow damage to have an effect on the performance of the vehicle. True to the spirit of the sport, cars even get dirty as they speed over muddy tracks towards the finish line.
entries.rom_name: Michelin Rally Masters - Race of Champions (USA) (En,Fr,Es) (Track 1).bin

entries.name: Metal Slug X (USA)
entries.description: The third title in SNK's Metal Slug series, Metal Slug X for the PlayStation is a port of the 1999 coin-op game, which itself was an enhanced version of Metal Slug 2. Choose from four characters, two male and two female, as you move from left to right trying to destroy everything in your path. Along the way, you can rescue hostages to earn points and acquire new weapon power-ups.

entries.name: Men in Black - The Series - Crashdown (USA)
entries.description: Take the first-person roles of Men In Black Jay and Kay to track down a good agent gone bad in this release based on the Warner Bros. animated series. Gameplay offers a mix of action and adventure, as player must explore over two dozen 3D New York locations and use ultra high-tech gadgets to neutralize the threats of 15 different alien species.
entries.rom_name: Men in Black - The Series - Crashdown (USA).bin

entries.name: Mega Man X6 (USA) (Rev 1)
entries.description: Mega Man X6 is yet another addition to the long-running Capcom franchise. Picking up immediately after the events in Mega Man X5, the Blue Bomber finds himself investigating recent reports of reploids running amok. Only he can save the reploids and avenge Zero's sacrifice. Following the same formula that the series' forefathers adhered to, this latest PlayStation incarnation sees Mega Man X traveling through eight levels, each of which houses a boss character whose weapon can be claimed by Mega Man X once defeated. As an added bonus, Mega Man X can now use Zero's sword throughout his adventure.

entries.name: Mega Man X5 (USA)
entries.description: The Reploid Wars of 21XX are mercifully over, but that doesn't mean all is safe with Earth and its orbiting colonies. Eurasia, the largest colony, has been taken over by mysterious terrorists, and its gravity device has been altered. Now, Eurasia is on a direct collision course with Earth, and could destroy the planet and all life (and robots) upon it.

entries.name: Mega Man X4 (USA)
entries.description: Mega Man X, the reploid leader of the 17th unit Maverick Hunters, and his best friend Zero have to stop a reploid rebellion. Each of them gets involved in a different way and you can play as either character through the parallel stories.

entries.name: Mega Man Legends 2 (USA)
entries.description: Mega Man has been around since the early 8-bit days, making him even older than some gamers. He returns to home video screens in Mega Man Legends 2. As in the immediately previous release Mega Man Legends, the hero who was once just a little blue sprite is now rendered in full 3D detail.

entries.name: Mega Man Legends (USA)
entries.description: In a world covered by endless water... People are forced to eke out a living on the small patches of land that remain above the sea. The people of this world rely on ancient technology driven by quantum refractors, a powerful energy source. These refractors lie in ancient ruins underground and in the sea and are sought out by explorers called Diggers. These brave explorers are the sole source of refractor energy which has become a cornerstone of the emerging civilizations. Originally, this was the Diggers' only purpose; to find refractors so that civilization would endure. However over the years, the story of an incredible treasure, the legendary Mother Lode, began to be whispered among the Diggers. The Mother Lode...a treasure so great that were it discovered, it would provide so much power that the world need never fear of running out of energy.

entries.name: Mega Man 8 (USA)
entries.description: Mega Man 8, known as Rockman 8: Metal Heroes in Japan, is a video game released by Capcom. It is the eighth installment in original Mega Man series, and was originally released in Japan on the Sony PlayStation on December 17, 1996. The following year, Mega Man 8 saw a release on the Sega Saturn and was localized for both consoles in North America and the PlayStation in PAL regions. Upon its release, Capcom reached the franchise's tenth anniversary. Mega Man 8 is the first game in the series made available on 32-bit consoles.

entries.name: MediEvil (USA)
entries.description: MediEvil tells the tale of Sir Daniel Fortesque, a man with a gift for storytelling. Though he never actually performed any of the wondrous deeds he so often boasted about, the king knighted him and appointed him as the head of the Royal Battalion. You see, the king liked stories, and truthful or not, Sir Daniel's stories were the best. Besides, Gallowmere hadn't seen a war in centuries...

entries.name: Medal of Honor - Underground (USA)
entries.description: The year is 1940, and the conquering force of the Third Reich has invaded France. Nazi Germany has marched into Paris and claimed the once proud nation as its own in its further quest for domination of Europe. The allied forces won't be coming to liberate France any time soon, as they have their hands full protecting Great Britain. The perception that the French have simply let Hitler walk into their country without a fight has not endeared the rest of the war-torn world to the cause.

entries.name: Medal of Honor (USA)
entries.description: The year is 1944. On the eve of what will be known ever after as the D-day invasion, the Air Transport Corps initiated the largest drop of troops yet seen by the Allied Forces. The plan couldn't have gone any worse: planes flew past their targets, those that came close were quickly shot down, and the inclement weather made it difficult to see where the pilots were heading. Yet in the midst of this colossal failure, a glimmer of hope emerged.

entries.name: MechWarrior 2 - 31st Century Combat - Arcade Combat Edition (USA)
entries.description: MechWarrior 2 gives you the chance to participate in the Clan Refusal War, a bloody civil war between the Clans that occurs after the Battle of Tukayyid. The Crusaders, led by Clan Jade Falcon, seek to launch another attack into the Inner Sphere. The Warden faction, led by Clan Wolf, believe that coexistence with the Inner Sphere is the best choice. The war will ultimately dictate which faction dominates the Clans.
entries.rom_name: MechWarrior 2 - 31st Century Combat - Arcade Combat Edition (USA) (Track 01).bin

entries.name: MDK (USA)
entries.description: MDK is a 3rd person action/shooter game in which the objective is to basically shoot everything that moves in six massive cities, each with their own sublevels. Because the world is being invaded by aliens, it is up to you and your sidekick Bones to stop the invasion and single handedly save Earth. In order to do so, you must make good use of your special suit, which allows you to do all kinds of things.

entries.name: Maximum Force (USA) (Beta)
entries.description: Maximum Force is a lightgun game for one or two players. As top counter-terrorism agents, you and a partner have three missions to complete to eradicate the world of a band of evil terrorists.

entries.name: Mat Hoffman's Pro BMX (USA)
entries.description: Following in the tradition of the Tony Hawk Pro Skater series comes Mat Hoffman's Pro BMX. Choose from eight different professional BMX players and go from course to course accomplishing goals and trick points.

entries.name: Master of Monsters - Disciples of Gaia (USA)
entries.description: Restricted by the laws of heaven, the gods had no choice but to sit back and watch the humans of Earthland destroy each other, their wars never seeming to cease. One day, however, the powerful Gaia had had enough. Along with six disciples, Gaia exited heaven in an attempt to set things straight on Earthland -- or so he led his disciples to believe. Upon his dissension, Gaia became greedy for power, summoning an army of monsters to parade with him throughout the entire world and locking his disciples into one of the many new magical towers he had constructed.
entries.rom_name: Master of Monsters - Disciples of Gaia (USA) (Track 1).bin

entries.name: Mass Destruction (USA)
entries.description: With little in the way of story elements, Mass Destruction's title alone tells you exactly what this game is about. Played throughout a scorched Earth, you'll shoot anything and everything in your path as you control one of three available tanks. Each tank has different armor and speed statistics: the Cheetah is a speedy tank built for hit and run operations; the Cobra lacks maneuverability but has highly destructive capabilities; and the Viper is an able firehouse without the armor capabilities of the Cobra.

entries.name: Mary-Kate and Ashley - Winners Circle (USA)
entries.description: Equestrian daydreams are virtually fulfilled in Mary-Kate and Ashley's Winner's Circle for the PlayStation console. The game offers a variety of activities and challenges for horse lovers and Olsen Twins fans alike. Players can ride as 3D-rendered incarnations of Mary-Kate or Ashley, or as their own custom-designed character.

entries.name: Mary-Kate and Ashley - Magical Mystery Mall (USA)
entries.description: Mary-Kate and Ashley's first PlayStation game takes them through a mall that is under the influence of a magical spell, which causes each of the stores to become a portal to another world. To right this terrible wrong, the twins must embark on an five-level adventure that involves choreographing music videos, modeling clothes, slinging burgers, taking pictures of boys, and even shredding the slopes on a snowboard.
entries.rom_name: Mary-Kate and Ashley - Magical Mystery Mall (USA) (Track 1).bin

entries.name: Mary-Kate and Ashley - Crush Course (USA)
entries.description: Mary-Kate and Ashley compete in a series of school-related activities to reveal their secret admirers in the aptly titled Crush Course for the PlayStation. As either Mary-Kate or Ashley Olsen, players decide on one of four outfits to wear before venturing off to school. The 'courses,' or activities, are spread across three halls, two of which are locked until the first is completed.

entries.name: Marvel vs. Capcom - Clash of Super Heroes (USA)
entries.description: It's the best of both worlds as the greatest superheroes of the Marvel Universe square off against the experienced warriors of Capcom's fighting and adventure games in this PlayStation adaptation of the Arcade hit.
entries.rom_name: Marvel vs. Capcom - Clash of Super Heroes (USA).bin

entries.name: Marvel Super Heroes vs. Street Fighter (USA)
entries.description: Capcom continues its crossover fighting series by pitting its Street Fighter characters against the likes of Spider-Man, Wolverine, Captain America, and Hulk. Choose from eight Marvel Super Heroes and nine Street Fighters before engaging the computer or a friend in combo-heavy action set amidst animated backdrops. Gameplay closely follows the format introduced in X-Men vs. Street Fighter on PlayStation. Battle a series of fighters in succession until the showdown with bosses Apocalypse and Cyber-Akuma. Six secret characters are also included, such as Mephisto and a metallic armored Spider-Man, though most are slight variants of existing combatants.
entries.rom_name: Marvel Super Heroes vs. Street Fighter (USA).bin

entries.name: Marvel Super Heroes (USA)
entries.description: Capcom aren't strangers in the 2D fighting realm; their Street Fighter series has dominated the market since its inception. Originally released in the Arcade, they're looking to dominate some more with Marvel Super Heroes.

entries.name: Martian Gothic - Unification (USA)
entries.description: The events begin in 11,000 BC when a meteorite from Mars strikes the Antarctic ice. It isn't until 1984 that it is discovered by mankind and labeled ALH 84001.
